title: Bulgogi
subtitle: Korean marinated beef cooked fast in a hot pan
excerpt: Thinly sliced sirloin marinated in soy, honey and grated pear, then cooked hot and fast until the edges caramelise. The pear breaks down the meat fibres so every slice is tender. Serve with rice and kimchi.
sourceNotes: Bulgogi means 'fire meat' in Korean and is one of the most popular Korean dishes worldwide. Grated Asian pear is traditional in the marinade for its tenderising enzymes.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate up to 24 hours for the most tender result.

content.text: Cook the beef in small batches over the highest heat you can manage. Too much meat in the pan at once drops the temperature and the beef steams rather than caramelises.

items.prepNote: sliced as thinly as possible, about 3mm

content.text: Freeze the beef for 30 minutes before slicing to make cutting thin strips easier.
Mix the soy sauce, honey, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, grated pear and gochugaru in a large bowl.
Add the beef slices and turn to coat. Cover and chill for at least 1 hour.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over the highest heat until just smoking.
Cook the beef in two or three batches. Spread in a single layer and cook for 1 to 2 minutes without stirring until the edges colour.
Toss once and cook for another 30 seconds. Remove and repeat with remaining beef.
Scatter with spring onion and serve immediately with steamed rice.

items.symptom: Beef is grey and steamed rather than caramelised.
items.cause: Too much beef in the pan at once.
items.fix: Cook in smaller batches; wipe pan between each.

items.cause: Honey caramelises quickly at high heat.
items.fix: Shake off excess marinade before adding beef to the pan.

items.cause: Slices were too thick or not marinated long enough.
items.fix: Slice thinner; marinate for a full hour minimum.
